Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
• 32-year-old* very active female (*age calculated from DOB 01 Jan 1980) with 2-week history of predominantly right-sided knee pain and intermittent clicking, provoked after ~20 min of running and during leg-extension exercises. No locking, giving-way, or persistent swelling; full range of motion on video assessment.  
• Most consistent with overuse/anterior knee pain syndrome.  
• Differential considerations (see summary below) include patellofemoral pain syndrome, patellar tendinopathy, early meniscal tear, iliotibial band syndrome; septic/inflammatory and thrombotic causes currently unlikely.  
• Management initiated: continue ice therapy; reduce running intensity; trial stronger prescribed NSAID (to be taken with food) in place of OTC ibuprofen; referral to physiotherapy for detailed knee examination and rehabilitation program; consider imaging (MRI) if poor progress or red-flag features emerge.  
• Safety-net advice provided—return urgently if persistent swelling, redness, heat, fever, or mechanical locking develops.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
1. Patellofemoral pain syndrome (runner’s knee) – High likelihood: onset after increased running, anterior/central knee pain, clicking with flexion-extension, normal ROM, no instability.  
2. Patellar tendinopathy – Moderate likelihood: activity-related pain with leg extension, responds to rest/ice.  
3. Degenerative/traumatic meniscal tear – Moderate likelihood: prior knee bruise, mechanical clicking; less likely due to absence of locking or persistent effusion.
